Why This Is Asked

Tests practical design of a per-tenant feature flag system in a CNF gateway stack, focusing on CRD design, a lean central policy API, and a sidecar with token authentication and caching.

Key Concepts

- Kubernetes CRD for per-tenant feature flags
- Sidecar fetch with short lived token and 60s cache
- Default semantics and tenant isolation
- End-to-end test in a single namespace

Code Example

```yaml
# Minimal CRD example
apiVersion: apiextensions.k8s.io/v1
kind: CustomResourceDefinition
metadata:
  name: featureflags.cnf.example.com
spec:
  group: cnf.example.com
  versions:
  - name: v1
    served: true
    storage: true
    schema:
      openAPIV3Schema:
        type: object
        properties:
          spec:
            type: object
            properties:
              perTenantFlags:
                type: object
              defaultEnabled:
                type: boolean

```

questions.explanation:
## Why This Is Asked
This question tests practical policy design at the intersection of CNF gateways, Kubernetes admission control, and SBOM-driven security. It requires translating per-tenant risk tolerances into enforceable constraints and verifying end-to-end behavior.

## Key Concepts
- Gatekeeper/OPA integration for admission control
- Per-namespace configuration and binding
- SBOM-driven vulnerability data (CVSS) attached to images
- Rego-based enforcement logic and concise ConstraintTemplates
- End-to-end testing: apply templates, constraints, and verify allow/deny outcomes

## Code Example
```yaml
# ConstraintTemplate: CNFImageVuln
apiVersion: templates.gatekeeper.sh/v1
kind: ConstraintTemplate
metadata:
  name: cnfimagevuln
spec:
  crd:
    spec:
      names:
        kind: CNFImageVuln
      scope: Cluster
  targets:
  - target: admission.k8s.gatekeeper.sh
    rego: |
      package cnfimagevuln
      violation[{"msg": msg}]
      # image.vulns is a list of {cve, cvss}
      violation[{"msg": msg}]
      {
        input.review.object.kind == "Deployment";
        ns := input.review.object.metadata.namespace;
        threshold := data.namespaceThresholds[ns];
        some i;
        vul := input.review.object.metadata.annotations["image.vulns"];
        cvss := vul[i].cvss;
        cvss > threshold; msg := sprintf("CVSS %v exceeds threshold %v for namespace %s", [cvss, threshold, ns]);
      }
```
```yaml
# Constraint: Bind per-namespace threshold
apiVersion: constraints.gatekeeper.sh/v1beta1
kind: CNFImageVuln
metadata:
  name: cnf-image-vuln-namespace
spec:
  namespaceSelector:
    matchExpressions:
    - {key: "cnf.namespace", operator: In, values: ["default"]}
```
```yaml
# Test manifest: should fail for CVSS > threshold and pass otherwise
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: test-cnf
  namespace: default
  annotations:
    image.vulns: "[{\"cve\":\"CVE-2024-0001\",\"cvss\":9}]"
spec:
  replicas: 1
  selector:
    matchLabels:
      app: test-cnf
  template:
    metadata:
      labels:
        app: test-cnf
    spec:
      containers:
      - name: app
        image: example/cnf:latest
```

## Follow-up Questions
- How would you handle multi-tenant overrides for temporary risk surges?
- How would you test performance impact of SBOM parsing in high-scale deployments?

## Why This Is Asked
Tests the ability to design observability systems with robust tenant isolation in CNF platforms, focusing on end-to-end tracing, data segmentation, and practical implementation.

## Key Concepts
- Distributed tracing fundamentals and W3C Trace Context
- Tenant-scoped attributes and resource naming conventions
- Telemetry routing strategies (tenant-based exporters, dedicated backends)
- Sampling strategies and their impact on observability versus cost

## Code Example
```yaml
# OpenTelemetry Collector config (minimal)
receivers:
  otlp:
    protocols:
      grpc: {}
exporters:
  otlp/tempo:
    endpoint: tempo:4317
    headers:
      x-tenant-id: "${TENANT_ID}"
processors:
  resource:
    attributes:
      - key: tenant_id
        value: "${TENANT_ID}"
        action: upsert
  batch: {}
service:
  pipelines:
    traces:
      receivers: [otlp]
      processors: [resource, batch]
      exporters: [otlp/tempo]
```

questions.explanation:
## Why This Is Asked

This question tests the ability to design tenant-isolated API validation using per-tenant OpenAPI specs, driven by a request header, within a CNF gateway. It emphasizes practical config storage, request validation, error handling, and observability.

## Key Concepts

- Per-tenant OpenAPI specs stored in ConfigMaps
- Tenant selection via X-TENANT-ID header
- Lightweight JSON validation using Ajv or similar
- Structured error responses (400) with detailed validation messages
- Audit logging for security and debugging
- Namespace-scoped manifests for isolation

## Code Example

```javascript
// Pseudo-validator flow:
// 1. Extract X-TENANT-ID header from request
// 2. Load corresponding OpenAPI spec from cnf.api.spec ConfigMap
// 3. Compile Ajv validator from spec
// 4. Validate request body and headers against schema
// 5. Return 400 with structured error if validation fails
// 6. Pass through to upstream service if valid
```

## Minimal YAML

```yaml
apiVersion: v1
kind: ConfigMap
metadata:
  name: cnf.api.spec
data:
  tenant-a.yaml: |-
    openapi: 3.0.0
    paths:
      /api/resource:
        post:
          requestBody:
            required: true
            content:
              application/json:
                schema:
                  type: object
                  required: [name]
                  properties:
                    name:
                      type: string
          responses:
            '200':
              description: Success
---
apiVersion: v1
kind: Service
metadata:
  name: api-gateway
spec:
  selector:
    app: gateway
  ports:
    - port: 8080
      targetPort: 8080
---
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: api-gateway
spec:
  replicas: 1
  selector:
    matchLabels:
      app: gateway
  template:
    metadata:
      labels:
        app: gateway
    spec:
      containers:
        - name: gateway
          image: nginx:1.21
          ports:
            - containerPort: 8080
          volumeMounts:
            - name: spec-config
              mountPath: /etc/cnf-specs
              readOnly: true
        - name: validator-sidecar
          image: validator:latest
          env:
            - name: SPEC_PATH
              value: /etc/cnf-specs
          volumeMounts:
            - name: spec-config
              mountPath: /etc/cnf-specs
              readOnly: true
      volumes:
        - name: spec-config
          configMap:
            name: cnf.api.spec
```

```yaml
# ConstraintTemplate (yaml)

kind: ConstraintTemplate
metadata:
  name: k8simageprovenance
spec:
  crd:
    spec:
      names:
        kind: K8sImageProvenance
  targets:
  - target: admission.k8s.gatekeeper.sh
    rego: |
      package k8simageprovenance
      violation[{"msg": msg}] {
        input.review.kind.kind == "Deployment"
        some c in input.review.object.spec.template.spec.containers

        msg := "image provenance missing or not tenant-approved"
      }
```

```yaml

apiVersion: constraints.gatekeeper.sh/v1beta1
kind: K8sImageProvenance

  parameters:
    allowedTenant: "tenant-a"
```

```yaml
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: tenant-a-gateway
  namespace: tenant-a
```

```yaml
apiVersion: argoproj.io/v1alpha1
kind: Rollout
metadata:
  name: gateway-rollout-tenant-a
spec:
  replicas: 3
  selector:
    matchLabels:
      app: gateway
      tenant: a
  template:
    metadata:
      labels:
        app: gateway
        tenant: a
    spec:
      containers:
      - name: gateway
        image: registry.example.com/cnf/gateway:latest
  strategy:
    canary:
      steps:
      - setWeight: 10
      - pause: { duration: 5m }
      - setWeight: 100
      analysis:
        templates:
        - templateName: canary-metrics
        metrics:
        - name: latency
          interval: 30s
          successCondition: result < 0.001 * 0.15
        - name: error-rate
          interval: 30s
          successCondition: result < 0.005
```

```yaml
apiVersion: argoproj.io/v1alpha1
kind: AnalysisTemplate
metadata:
  name: canary-metrics
spec:
  metrics:
  - name: latency
    provider:
      prometheus:
        url: http://prometheus.k8s.svc
        query: sum(rate(http_request_duration_seconds_sum[5m])) / sum(rate(http_request_duration_seconds_count[5m]))
  - name: error-rate
    provider:
      prometheus:
        url: http://prometheus.k8s.svc
        query: sum(rate(http_requests_total{status!~"2.."}[5m]))
```

questions.explanation:
## Why This Is Asked
Tests the ability to implement gatekeeping for image provenance at the namespace boundary, using Cosign and SBOM, with a small, config-driven policy store.

## Key Concepts
- Cosign signing and SBOM attachment
- ImagePolicyWebhook basics
- ConfigMap as policy store
- Namespace provenance validation
- Minimal test manifests

## Code Example
```javascript
// Minimal policy snippet (conceptual)
apiVersion: imagepolicy.k8s.io/v1alpha1
kind: ImageReview
spec:
  imagePattern: "*"
  requiredAnnotations:
    - cosignSignature
    - sbomDigest
  provenance:
    namespaceLabel:
      key: "cnf-tenant/org"
      value: "acme"
```

```javascript
// Minimal test manifest (conceptual)
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: test-gateway
  namespace: tenant-a
spec:
  template:
    spec:
      containers:
      - name: gateway
        image: registry.example.com/acme/gateway:1.0.0
```
